title: The call from Joe Glaser to join Louis
summary: Glaser phoned him at Disneyland while Barney Bigard was leaving; Joe gave two weeks' notice and joined Louis in Ontario in July, staying until July 29, 1964.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Tell me about how you got the offer with Louis.
That's where I'm going. We hadn't played two weeks at Disneyland until Louis called me -- at least his manager did.
Where did they call you? At home?
About a year before, I'd sat in for Barney on a couple of deals with Louis' band, and Louis told me at the time that he wanted me if Barney left. So anyway, I got this call at Disneyland...
Yes, they called me at... Joe Glaser called me.
Well, one of the managers at the park called me, told me it was a very important call from New York. And when I got off the boat, they had the number -- "You call this number collect."
Oh, that's right. You were on the boat. Of course, sorry.

See? And when I got off the boat, I knew then and there it must have been that. Because for some reason, I heard Barney was leaving. And I called Joe, and I told Joe, I said, "You know I'm working at Disneyland, and I have to give a two weeks' notice." I said, "Sure, of course I want to come with Louis, providing the money is all right"

and everything like that.
So we made the arrangements, and I joined Louis in
July, something like July 4, I believe, or something like
that.

I joined Louis in Bala(?), Ontario,
Canada. That was my first date with them. And from then
on, needless to say, I stayed with him until July 29th (I
think), 1964.

A little over three years. And during
that time, that's when he made "Hello Dolly."
